newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's El Al sees 1996 loss of $100 million.
newsitem.headline: Israel's El Al sees 1996 loss of $100 million.

text.p: El Al Israel Airlines said a decline in tourism caused by Middle East violence will cause the state-owned airline to make an estimated loss of $100 million in 1996, its first loss in 10 years.
"The sharp drop in tourism to Israel has severely affected our operations," airline president Yoel Feldshuh said.

The national carrier, which made a net profit of $15 million in 1995, will officially report results next year but Feldshuh told a news conference late on Wednesday that preliminary estimates put the loss at around $100 million.

Tourism has dropped sharply this year after a series of suicide bombings in February and March, fighting between Israel and Hizbollah guerrillas based in Lebanon in April and the recent TWA crash in the United States.
New bookings for the rest of the year are also low following increased tension between Israelis and Palestinians, with clashes in September claiming 75 lives.
Feldshuh said other contributing factors to the expected loss included a sharp rise in jet fuel prices in recent months, a strong local currency and competition on flights in and out of Israel.
Last year the state-owned airline reported revenues of $1.22 billion and flew a record three million passengers.
Feldshuh took over from Rafi Harlev at the beginning of October. Harlev resigned in June saying at the time he was unhappy with the government's inability to privatise the airline.
Feldshuh said he supported privatisation but noted that short-term prospects were not good because of the airline's loss. El Al has been profitable for the past 10 years.
